reference.use: Study the deadpan narrator, the chant tied to visible actions and the payoff in the picture; do not reuse the family photo gag.

origin.what: A format the owner found on a reel and wrote his own script for on 2026-11-18: the 'While they're out partying btw' and 'huss huss huss' memes told as a one-and-three-quarter-minute story. His corrections to our first draft are the rules of the topic.
origin.owner: its IRL coated with minecraft. No nether, no mc shenanigans. its a recreation cmon.

premise.oneLiner: A real, everyday skill done far too seriously by a block-town character, told with the breathy HUS HUS HUS meme. The skill must change the story, not just decorate a montage.
mustHave: The first two seconds show the real skill in action and its readable result, with the premise clear muted.
One identifiable ordinary skill is overtrained through visible, distinct attempts and failures.
Every on-screen performance of the HUS skill has the matching HUS breaths; the chant marks actual actions, not generic montage filler.
An original real-life problem and payoff; the practiced skill has a visible consequence.
The lead treats the disproportionate practice seriously; the comedy comes from the contrast and the images.
Keep spoken gaps at or under 1.9 seconds; use pictures and action to carry quieter beats.
never: game mechanics, Nether, mobs, lava, crafting, or Minecraft jokes: the real world is recreated with block people and places.
reuse another film’s lines, gag, characters, or exact story; especially do not retell the family-photo / four-ears plot of the approved Elbow reference.
begin on a face, title card, or narration instead of the skill in action.
make the lead knowingly play the dedication as a joke.

formats.approved-elbow: The first approved HUS film starts with an awkward family photo, then turns practiced posing into a solution and an unrelated final-image joke. Its seven-scene storyboard is a model of action-to-chant and a visual payoff, not a plot template.
formats.owner-origin: The cook / party / job / reunion outline in origin.page is one format, not a mandatory plot. The barber is an unreviewed first build that supplies reusable production assets.

camera.note: Hard cuts. A script line with action under it is cut into several pictures with `cut:`.

film.shortsRule: Keep the vertical film well under 3:00. Working target and hard limits below are retained from the current Recreation contract; the approved 77.50 s Elbow film is a measured reference, not a duration quota.

models.thats-me-the-elbow: The approved HUS reference: film, source, shot sheet and measured review in Topics/Recreation/Hus hus reference.
models.note: The owner-approved Elbow film is the comedy, action/chant and visual-payoff reference; its story is not reusable. The barber is an unreviewed first build with reusable room and shop parts. The cook / parties outline is the owner’s originating example, not a mandatory plot.

sound.note: Use an original score, not the In This Town track. The approved HUS mix is measured in reference.measured and in the archived source/sound.lock.json; the ranges here are working limits.
